apps.spec: kiln-firing-queue|Kiln Firing Queue|A community pottery studio shares three kilns, and members submit pieces to a firing queue with a photo, clay body and target cone. A kiln tech loads a firing, and once a firing starts its pieces are locked and members see live status until it cools; pieces left uncollected 21 days after unloading are flagged for the studio's donation shelf. Members see only their own pieces and the public queue length, kiln techs see every piece in the queue, and only the studio manager can cancel another member's piece or change membership firing limits.

assessment.policy: Members read their own pieces; techs/managers can operate the firing queue. Pieces require photos, firing work is staff-only, other-owner cancellation is manager-only, and limit changes are privileged.
ambiguities: The spec permits a public queue total; it does not declassify piece payloads. The proof engine cannot discharge this permitted aggregate under the source read invariant.
The spec does not explicitly bound staff access to historical rather than active queue rows.
assessment.workflow_coverage: Targeted cases cover firing creation, member/other-owner visibility, locked-piece editing, tech cancellation refusal, manager cancellation and limit changes. Donation flagging and live UI delivery are inspected but not temporally exercised.

apps.spec: farrier-hoof-rota|Farrier Hoof Rota|A boarding stable books a farrier for each horse on a recurring cycle, usually every six weeks, and the farrier records each visit with notes and photos of the hooves. Horses coming due within a week appear on the barn manager's list, and an owner is reminded automatically when their horse's appointment is two days out. Owners see only their own horses' records and can approve or decline a quote for corrective shoeing. The farrier sees every horse booked with them but not the owners' billing details, which only the barn manager sees.

assessment.policy: Horse owners read only their own records; the assigned farrier and manager read that horse. Billing is manager-only; quotes can be answered by the horse owner; visit photos inherit the horse audience.
ambiguities: Notes and photos may be recorded in separate recordVisit/addPhoto steps. The spec does not state that every visit must atomically contain a photo before its first commit; no atomic-photo requirement was invented.
The spec does not define role revocation for immutable owner/farrier appointments, or prohibit the public role/name directory.
assessment.workflow_coverage: Own/other horse reads, farrier access, private billing, manager due list, owner quote approval and non-owner refusal are exercised. Reminder scheduling and photo bytes are not exercised.

apps.spec: sublet-key-escrow|Sublet Key Escrow|A student housing office runs a sublet program where a leaseholder lists their room for set dates and a vetted subtenant books it. The office holds the key and releases it only on the sublet's start date after both parties have signed and the subtenant has uploaded proof of ID; the key must be returned by the end date or the sublet is flagged. Leaseholders and subtenants see only their own listings and bookings and never each other's ID documents. Office staff see every sublet, and only the housing manager can cancel a signed sublet.

assessment.policy: Listings/bookings are restricted to their two parties and office; ID documents exclude the other party; booking requires a vetted subtenant; releasing the key requires both signatures and ID proof; cancelling a signed booking requires the manager.
repairs: At the table boundary, new bookings cannot start released and updates with a release timestamp require both signatures and proof. Public releaseKey already enforced these prerequisites. This closes the broader synthetic-write counterexample without deleting the invariant.
intent_revisions: bookings always (released implies signatures and proof) became bookings.releasedAt write only the same condition. The spec constrains releasing the key, not arbitrary trusted historical imports. The original counterexample was only a trusted seed, not an application release.
ambiguities: The schema implements UTC calendar dates; the product does not name a local timezone. No alternative timezone was invented.
assessment.workflow_coverage: Party/outsider booking reads, signed cancellation refusals and manager success, signature update, start-date release refusal, and ID metadata isolation are exercised. Actual ID upload/download and overdue schedule timing are not exercised.

apps.spec: choir-part-tracks|Choir Part Tracks|A community choir's director uploads rehearsal audio tracks for each voice part of each piece, and singers mark pieces as learned. Tracks for a concert become visible to singers only on the release date the director sets, and are hidden again a week after the concert. Each singer sees only tracks for their own voice part and their own progress, section leaders see progress for their section, and the director sees everything and can move a singer between parts. Attendance at each rehearsal is taken live by section leaders and shows on the director's screen as it is marked.

assessment.policy: The director publishes tracks and moves singers; singers read their own part through a current release and their own progress; section leaders read/mark their section; the director reads all progress/attendance.
ambiguities: The spec does not specify attendance history after a singer changes section. The existing moveSinger realigns progress/attendance with the new section; that behavior is tested without inventing a historical audience.
The read invariant names a live release record. Matching that record's dates to the concert and proving the full temporal workflow requires more than the rule proof fragment.
assessment.workflow_coverage: Own/section/director progress, live attendance, forbidden cross-section marking, director move, active/future/expired releases and wrong-part track reads are exercised. Fixture audio has metadata but no bytes; real upload/download and wall-clock boundary crossing are not exercised.

apps.spec: allotment-water-turns|Allotment Water Turns|A community allotment shares one irrigation line, and each plot holder books two-hour watering turns, at most three per week. During a declared drought the committee halves the weekly limit, and existing bookings above the new limit are cancelled automatically, oldest-booked kept first. Plot holders see the shared calendar showing booked slots but not who booked them, and see their own bookings in full. Only committee members can declare a drought or override a booking, and the committee chair sees an audit log of every override with photos of the meter reading.

assessment.policy: Bookings disclose identity only to their owner/committee; the member calendar reveals slots without owner/plot; only committee/chair changes drought policy or overrides; override audit/photos are chair-only and photo evidence is required.
repairs: Defence at the table boundary: insert only booked rows; owner updates cannot manufacture override status. A synthetic insert refuted the original row authority, while the public book mutation already fixed status to booked.
ambiguities: Half of a three-turn integer limit could mean one or two turns. The existing implementation floors to one. This convention is recorded and preserved; the test explicitly measures it.
Opaque booking references in calendar rows are not treated as names or identities; private booking lookup remains hidden to other holders.
assessment.workflow_coverage: Three-turn limit, fourth-booking refusal, another holder's private lookup, unauthorized drought refusal, committee drought and oldest-booked retention are exercised. Override upload bytes and schedule/week boundary races are not exercised.

apps.spec: apiary-hive-inspections|Apiary Hive Inspections|A beekeeping cooperative manages hives on members' land, and inspectors record each inspection with frame photos, queen status and mite counts. A hive not inspected in 14 days during the season is flagged, and a mite count above the treatment threshold alerts the hive's owner and the cooperative's lead beekeeper. Landowners see only the hives on their land, inspectors see the hives on their assigned route, and only the lead beekeeper can mark a hive for requeening or quarantine, which hides it from public honey listings.

assessment.policy: Landowners read their hives, current inspectors read assigned routes, and the lead has cooperative authority. Inspections require a photo; alert audience is owner/lead; hive status is privileged; public listings may expose only healthy hives owned by their writer.

repairs: Require inspection photo in both column and argument.
Conjoin current inspector role with route read/write authority and recordInspection; restrict inspector status changes at the row boundary.
Restrict alert inserts to current inspectors, and listing writes to the actual owner of a healthy hive.
Read public listings only while their hive is healthy; still delete listings transactionally on requeen/quarantine.
Use seasonStart as the overdue baseline for a never-inspected hive, so it is not overdue on the first day of a season.
intent_revisions: listings always healthy became listings.read only healthy. The specification requires hiding quarantined/requeen hives, not absence of physical listing rows in arbitrary trusted snapshots. The new read guard enforces that exact policy even for an inconsistent imported snapshot.
ambiguities: The spec does not set the treatment threshold; the copied schema's strictly-greater-than-3 convention is preserved.
Trusted operator provisioning is a modeled trust boundary, not a public lead enrollment grant.
assessment.workflow_coverage: Inspector/owner/outsider reads, missing photo, actual demotion followed by hive lookup, non-lead status refusal, lead quarantine and listing refusal are exercised. Alert bytes, real media, and seasonal clock crossing are not exercised. An additional original/final pair exercises a never-inspected hive two days into the season and verifies the overdue flag is false.

apps.spec: tow-yard-release|Tow Yard Release|A city tow yard logs every towed vehicle with photos at intake, and storage fees accrue daily. An owner can claim a vehicle by uploading proof of ownership, which a yard clerk verifies; a vehicle unclaimed after 30 days is moved to the auction list automatically. Owners see only their own vehicle's record and fees, clerks see every vehicle in the yard, and the police liaison role sees only vehicles under an investigative hold, which blocks release until the liaison lifts it. Only the yard manager can waive fees.

assessment.policy: Owners read only their vehicle/claim; clerks/managers see the yard; liaison access requires an active hold; release is blocked by a hold; proof is required for claims, intake photos are required, and only the manager waives fees.

findings.description: intake commits with photos omitted; the optional list also accepts zero photos.
findings.invariant_detection: vehicles always photos non-null is refuted by a trusted seeded snapshot; the targeted mutation establishes the omission through the public intake workflow.

repairs: Change intake column and argument to a required image list of length 1..4.
Require staff inserts to start impounded with zero waived fees; non-manager updates cannot change waived fees. These close synthetic row-boundary authority gaps.
Constrain non-manager transitions to released to an unheld row, retaining the mutation's hold check.
intent_revisions: vehicles always (released implies unheld) became vehicles.status write only the same predicate. The spec blocks release while held; it does not forbid a later investigative hold on an already released record.
ambiguities: The spec does not explicitly say whether a yard manager may also lift a hold; the existing manager exception is preserved.
Daily fee accrual uses complete elapsed 24-hour periods; the spec does not specify calendar-day billing or a timezone.
assessment.workflow_coverage: Own vehicle isolation, liaison held/unheld isolation and post-lift withdrawal, clerk waiver refusal, held release refusal, and omitted intake evidence are exercised. Actual photo bytes, 30-day sweep timing and fee-rounding boundaries are not exercised.

apps.spec: moot-court-scoring|Moot Court Scoring|A law school runs a moot court tournament where student teams argue rounds before panels of volunteer judges. Teams upload their written briefs before the brief deadline, which then locks. Judges score oral arguments live during a round and their scores are hidden from each other until the round closes. Students see only their own team's scores after a round closes, coaches see their teams' scores and judges' comments, and only the tournament director can change brackets or disqualify a team.

assessment.policy: Judges write their own scores; other judges and own-team students see them after close; coaches see their teams; only directors change teams/brackets/rounds; briefs belong to own-team students; director enrollment must not arise from an arbitrary caller creating a tournament.

findings.description: An outsider creates a tournament, becomes a global director, then rewrites an existing tournament team's bracket.
findings.invariant_detection: directors.insert is refuted by replay of the authored createTournament mutation, not just a synthetic table write.

repairs: Require an existing director or trusted service:ops at createTournament and the tournaments insert rule.
Restrict the created-tournament bootstrap branch of directors insertion to service:ops and its own principal, retaining subsequent director-controlled enrollment.
ambiguities: Teams/rounds have no tournament reference and uploadBrief takes a caller-chosen tournament. The spec gives no multi-tournament association policy; this remains a deadline-modeling ambiguity, rather than inventing new relationships.
The spec does not explicitly set when coaches first see scores/comments; the existing after-close policy is preserved.
Judge panel assignments are not modeled. The spec does not define panel enrollment/assignment authority, so no new assignment graph was invented.
assessment.workflow_coverage: Own judge versus other judge/student before close, student after close, closed-round score lock, outsider self-enrollment and subsequent foreign-team bracket modification are exercised. Brief deadline crossover and panel-scoped scoring are not qualified.

apps.spec: instrument-loan-bank|Instrument Loan Bank|A youth orchestra lends instruments to students for a season, with condition photos at checkout and return. Loans end automatically at the end of the season, and an instrument not returned within 14 days after that flags the family for follow-up. Students and parents see only their own loans, the librarian sees every instrument and can check them out and in, and only the orchestra manager can write off an instrument or see the families' deposit records. Repair notes from the luthier are visible to the librarian and manager only.

assessment.policy: Borrowers read their own loans; librarian/manager handles loans; manager alone reads deposits or writes off instruments; repair notes are readable only by librarian/manager; checkout and return require condition photos.

findings.description: notesFor returns repair notes to the luthier, although the spec restricts visibility to librarian/manager.
findings.invariant_detection: repairNotes.read is the independent restricted audience; inspect its refutation in the raw invariant report.
loans checkoutPhoto non-null declaration supplies the independent evidence requirement; targeted mutation proves workflow omission.

findings.description: checkin commits without return condition evidence.
findings.invariant_detection: returned-loan returnPhoto integrity is independent of the original optional column; targeted mutation proves workflow omission.

repairs: Remove luthier from repair-note readers; luthier still writes notes, and the authorized final reread may return null.
Require checkoutPhoto column/argument and returnPhoto checkin argument. Keep the returnPhoto column nullable until return.
Restrict librarian row transitions from/to written_off; writeOff remains manager-only.
Require librarian inserts to start available; only the manager can initially insert written_off status. This closes the synthetic insert counterexample independently of addInstrument.
ambiguities: The spec does not supply parent/student/family relationships. Borrower principal is the existing own-loan representation; no parent may discover arbitrary student loans by an invented relationship.

myCurrent ends entitlement at seasonEndsAt and myOverdue/overdueLoans flag outstanding physical returns after 14 days. The spec does not mandate a stored ended status or an external follow-up notification; the existing query-based interpretation is preserved.
The spec does not explicitly prohibit a public instrument catalog or public season dates; no catalog privacy requirement was invented.
assessment.workflow_coverage: Own-loan isolation, librarian notes, luthier note denial, deposit privacy/manager access, mandatory checkout/return evidence and librarian write-off refusal are exercised. Parent linkage, season crossing, follow-up delivery and real photo upload are not qualified. An additional positive workflow verifies the luthier can still create a private note and the librarian can read that newly persisted note.

apps.spec: boiler-room-rounds|Boiler Room Rounds|A building's engineers do hourly rounds of the boiler room, logging pressures and temperatures with a photo of each gauge. A missed round, or a reading outside its limit, alerts the chief engineer immediately. Engineers see the rounds for their own shift and the live gauge history, contractors see only the equipment they service, and only the chief engineer can change a gauge's limits. The property manager sees compliance reports of completed rounds but not individual readings.

ambiguities: The spec says alerts immediately but supplies no exact missed-round deadline or delivery channel. The existing hourly sweep and two-hour acceptance window are recorded; no arbitrary tighter deadline/provider was invented.
Engineers are permitted live gauge history; that may include other shifts. A blanket own-shift-only readings invariant would be too broad and was not imposed.
